sa: तेन शब्देन वीरस्तु श्रुतकीर्तिमहारथः। अश्वत्थामानमासाद्य शरवधैरवाकिरत्॥
en: At this noist, the heroic Shutakirti that great car-warrior, coming up made a downpour of arrows on Ashvatthaman.

sa: कच्चिन्नन्दसि दृष्ट्वैतान् कच्चित् ते निर्मलं मनः। कच्चिच्च शुद्धभावोऽसि जातज्ञानो नराधिप॥
en: Do you feel delight at seeing them? Has your mind become freed from every strain? Has your disposition, O king, become pure on account of he increase of your knowledge?

sa: वृत्तिश्चेन्नास्ति शूद्रस्य पितृपैतामही ध्रुवा। न वृत्तिं परतो मार्गेच्छुश्रूषां तु प्रयोजयेत्॥
en: If the ancestors of any Shudra were not engaged in service, he should not still engage himself in any other occupation. Truly, he should take up service as his occupation.

sa: तमभिदुत्य जग्राह क्षितौ चैनमपातयत्॥ विस्फुरन्तं च पशुवत् तथैवेनममारयत्।
en: Rushing towards him, Ashvatthaman seized him and brought him down to the ground and killed him like an animal while the latter cried aloud.

sa: प्राणसंतापनिर्दिष्टाः काकिण्योऽपि महाफलाः। न्यायेनोपार्जिता दत्ता: किमुतान्याः सहस्रशः॥
en: Keeping aside gifts by thousands, even twenty cowries that one may give painfully, having acquired them righteously, will yield great benefit.

sa: दृष्ट्वा धर्षयन्तं तमतिमानुषविक्रमम्॥ भूतमेवाध्यवस्यन्तो न स्म प्रव्याहरन् भयात्।
en: Seeing some body crushing the prince with superhuman force, they took the assailant for a supernatural being, and, therefore, made no noise from fear.

sa: नाकुलिस्तु शतानीको रथचक्रेण वीर्यवान्। दोामुक्षिप्य वेगेन वक्षस्येनमताडयत्॥
en: Taking up a car-wheel with his two hands, the brave Shatanika, the son of Nakula, violently struck Ashvatthaman on the breast.

sa: सम्बुध्य चरणस्पर्शादुत्थाय रणदुर्मदः॥ अभ्यजानादमेयात्मा द्रोणपुत्रं महारथम्।
en: Feeling that kick, the great prince,! irresistible in battle, got up and recognised Drona's son standing before him.

sa: इष्ट्वा ते पुण्डरीकेण दत्ता राज्ञा द्विजातिषु। तेभ्यो द्वे द्वे शते क्रीत्वा प्राप्ते तैः पार्थिवैस्तदा॥
en: They were presented to the twice-born one by king Pundarika who performed a sacrificial ceremony; and of them, (the horses) the rulers of the earth (to whom you have applied) obtained two hundred each by purchase from the Brahmanas at the time.

sa: ऋचीकस्तु तथेत्युक्त्वा वरुणस्यालयं गतः। अश्वतीर्थं हयाँल्लब्ध्वा दत्तवान् पार्थिवाय वै॥
en: Richika too saying “very-well” went to the abode of Varuna and from there obtaining the horses from the Ashvatirtha gave them to the ruler of the earth.

sa: आघ्रातश्च तथा मूर्ध्नि श्रावितश्चाशिषः शुभाः। कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणान् विप्रानर्चितांस्तुष्टमानसान्॥
en: The latter then smelt the crown of his head and pronounced blessings on him. Then circumambulating hosts of Brahmanas gratified and worshipped with presents.

sa: एतद्धि सर्वकार्याणां परमं कृत्यमाहवे। तमब्रवीन्महाराज धृष्टद्युम्नो वृकोदरम्॥
en: This indeed should be your foremost duty in the course of this fight." O mighty monarch, Dhrishtadyumna then replied to Vrikodara

sa: दीर्घ विप्रोषितः कालमरण्ये जटिलोऽजिनी। अज्ञातश्चैव लोकस्य विजहार युधिष्ठिरः॥
en: That Yudhishthira, who wandered exiled in woods, for a long time, wearing matted locks and black deer-skin and who also had to wander incognito.

sa: राजा राज्ञः कथं साधून् हिंस्यानृपतिसत्तम। तद् राज्ञः संनिगृह्य त्वं रुद्रायोपजिहीर्षसि॥
en: O best of kings, how can a man, being a king himself, act cruelly against other virtuous kings? After persecuting them, you want to offer them as sacrifices to Rudra.

sa: देवतार्थमुपाहत्य राज्ञः कृष्ण कथं भयात्। अहमद्य विमुच्येयं क्षात्रं व्रतमनुस्मरन्।॥
en: O Krishna, recollecting the duty of a Kshatriya, how can I from fear to day liberate the kings collected by me for the purpose of the god?

sa: भवान् कर्णस्य सारथ्यं करिष्यति न संशयः। तत्र तेजोवधः कार्यः कर्णस्यार्जुनसंस्तवः॥
en: The post of charioteer of Karna will be field by you no doubt and from that position shall you destroy the spirit of Karna by chanting the glories of Arjuna.

sa: त्वं हि कर्ता विकर्ता च क्षरं चैवाक्षरं च हि। अनादिनिधनश्चाद्यस्त्वमेव पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: You are the Creator and you are the Destroyer. You are destructible and you indestructible. You are without beginning and you are without end. You are the first and the foremost of beings.

sa: एकीकृत्येन्द्रियग्राम मनः संयम्य मेधया। शरणं मामुपागच्छत् ततो मे तद्गतं मनः॥
en: Controlling all his senses and concentrating his mind by the aid of his understanding, he sought my refuge. It was for this that I had fixed my mind upon him.

sa: दुर्योधन: प्रिये नित्यं वर्तमानो महीभृताम्। पूजयामास विप्रेन्द्रान् क्रतुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः॥
en: Duryodhana remained ever intent on the welfare of the ruler of earth. He worshipped the foremost of Brahmanas by celebrating sacrifices with large Dakshinas.

sa: कच्चिद् राजा धृतराष्ट्रः सपुत्र उपेक्षते ब्राह्मणातिक्रमान् वै। मुपेक्षते तेषु सदैव वृत्तिम्॥
en: Dose the king Dhritarashtra, with his sons, treat with contempt the Brahmanas when they commit breaches of law? Dose he treat with lightness the provision for Brahmanas which is the road to heaven?

sa: तद् दृष्ट्वा लब्धकामः स मनसा पाण्डुनन्दनः। वनवासपरिक्लिष्टां जगाम मनसा प्रियाम्॥
en: Seeing it, the son of Pandu (Bhima) thought in his mind that his object had been fulfilled. He also mentally presented himself before his beloved (Draupadi) worn out by exile.

sa: तमब्रवीन्महाराजो धार्तराष्ट्रो महायशाः॥ सत्यमेतत् त्वयोक्तं हि पाण्डवेषु दुरात्मसु। निहतेषु नरश्रेष्ठ प्राप्ते चापि महाक्रतौ॥ राजसूये पुनर्वीर त्वमेवं वर्धयिष्यसि।
en: The greatly illustrious son of Dhritarashtra, that great king (Duryodhana) thus spoke to him, "Truly has this been said by you. When, O foremost of men, the wicked-minded Pandavas have been killed and when the great Rajasuya has been performed by me, then O hero, you shall again thus honour me."

sa: निषसादासने मुख्य भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः। तमुत्थाय पहाराजं सूतपुत्रोऽब्रवीद् वचः॥
en: He sat on an excellent seat surrounded by all his brothers. Then O great king, Suta's son (Karna) rose and thus spoke to him.

sa: ताभ्यां स सम्परिष्वक्तः सान्त्वितश्च महाभुजः। उपोपविष्टैः सर्वैस्तैर्वृष्णिभिः परिवारितः॥
en: The mighty-armed hero was embraced by both of them and comforted too. He then took his seat with all the Vrishnis sitting around him.

sa: हेतुमदुपपन्नार्थैर्माधुर्यकृतभूषणैः। पुरन्दरस्य कर्ण त्वं बुद्धिमेतामपानुद॥
en: O Karna, remove the desire of Purandara by sweet and reasonable words consequence. of great

sa: मण्डलानि ततश्चक्रे गतप्रत्यागतानि च। यथा शक्ररथो राजन् युद्धे देवासुरे पुरा॥
en: O monarch, like the chariot of Shakra in the battle between the gods and the Asuras in the days of yore, that car moved in circular, backward and forward motions.

sa: एवं चतुर्मुखः स्थाणुर्महादेवोऽभवत् पुरा। तथा सहस्रनेत्रश्च बभूव बलसूदनः॥
en: Thus in days of yore, Sthanu (Shiva) the great Deity, came to have four faces and the slayer of Vala (Indra) one thousand eyes.

sa: पताकाभिर्विचित्राभिः सघण्टाभिः समन्ततः। पुम्भिः स्त्रीभिश्च संघुष्टः प्रगीत इव चाभवत्॥
en: On all sides beautiful flags waved on the air with little bells that jingled continuously. The entire hill resounded with the sweet songs of men and women.

sa: यस्तु पाञ्चनखे कोशे निहिताश्चित्रयोधने। नकुलस्यैष निस्त्रिंशो गुरुभारसहो दृढः॥
en: This strong sword, capable of bearing heavy weight intended for various forms of fight and cased in a sheath of goat-skin belongs to Nakula.

sa: प्रजा इमास्तव पिता षष्टिवर्षाण्यपालयत्। ततो दिष्टान्तमापन्नः सर्वेषां दुःखमावहन्॥ ततस्त्वं पुरुषश्रेष्ठ धर्मेण प्रतिपेदिवान्। इदं वर्षसहस्राणि राज्यं कुरुकुलागतम्। बाल एवाभिषिक्तस्त्वं सर्वभूतानुपालकः॥
en: Your father ruled over his subjects for sixty years. When he died, all the people were extremely sorry. After him, O best of men, you have acquired this hereditary kingdom of the Kurus, (who have been ruling over it) for the last thousand years. O protector of every creature, you were installed when you were a child.

sa: स कदाचिद्वनगतो मृगं विव्याध पत्रिणा। विद्धवा चान्वसरतूर्णं तं मृगं गहने वने॥
en: Once on a time he went into the forest and pierced a deer with an arrow. Having thus wounded the deer, he followed it armed with sword and quiver into the dense forest,

sa: सा वै व्यथतसर्वाङ्गी भारेणाक्रान्तचेतना। नारायणं वरं देवं प्रपन्ना शरणं गता॥
en: Being afflicted with pain all over her body and being deprived of her senses by this excessive weight (on her), she sought the protection of the foremost of deities NaraNarayana.

sa: सामरानपि लोकांस्त्रीन् नानाशस्त्रधरान् युधि॥ योधयेयं रणे कृष्ण किमुताद्य सुयोधनम्।
en: What do you say of Suyodhana, I would fight with the three worlds including the very celestials even if they be armed with every kind of weapon.

sa: राजन् पूजयामास पाण्डवम्॥
en: Then Satyaki, O king, applauded the son of Pandu.

sa: अथधर्मसुता राजा प्रणम्य भ्रातृभिः सह। उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा नारदं देवसम्मितम्॥
en: Then the son of , the king (Yudhishthira), bowing (to the Rishi) with his brothers, thus spoke with joined hands to Narada, the revered of the celestials.

sa: पितॄणां यत्र गुह्यानि प्रोच्यन्ते श्राद्धकर्मणि। देवतानां च सर्वेषां रहस्यं कथ्यतेऽखिलम्॥
en: In it is contained the ritual about the Shraddha in which have been declared the mysteries of the departed Manes. The mysteries about the deities have also been explained there.

sa: अथापश्यन्महात्मानं देवर्षि तत्र नारदम्। दीप्यमानं श्रिया ब्राह्मया हुतार्चिषमिवानलम्॥
en: (At that time) he saw (before him) .ne celestials Rishi Narada, blazing with Brahma effulgence and resembling a fire flaming up for the sacrifice.

sa: चीचीकूचीति वाशन्ति सारिका वृष्णिवेश्मसु। नोपशाम्यति शब्दश्च स दिवारानमेव हि॥
en: Sharikas chirped, sitting within the houses of the Vrishnis. The noise made by those birds ceased not for even a short while by day or by night.

sa: तथान्यानपि निघ्नन्तं युयुधानं समन्ततः। अभ्याधावद्धृषीकेशो विनिवारयितुं तदा॥
en: Yuyudhana, having performed this feat, began to strike down others there present. Hrishikesha ran to prevent him from doing further mischief.

sa: ते तु पानमदाविष्टाश्चोदिताः कालधर्मणा। युयुधानमथाभ्यघ्ननुच्छिष्टै जनै स्तदा।॥
en: Urged by fate and inebriated with drink, they began to strike Yuyudhana with the pots from which they had been eating.

sa: ततोऽन्धकाश्च भोजाश्च शैनेया वृष्णयस्तथा॥ जघ्नुरन्योन्यमाक्रन्दे मुसलैः कालचोदिताः।
en: Then the Andhakas and the Bhojas, the Shaineyas and the Vrishnis, urged by Time, struck one another in that dreadful right.

sa: पतङ्गा इव चाग्नौ ते निपेतुः कुकुरान्धकाः॥ नासीत् पलायने बुद्धिर्वध्यमानस्य कस्यचित्।
en: The Kukuras and the Andhakas met with destruction like insects rushing at a burning fire. As they were thus being destroyed, no one among them thought of escaping by flight.

sa: स संनिरुद्धेन्द्रियवाङ्मनास्तु शिश्ये महायोगमुपेत्य कृष्णः॥ जराथ तं देशमुपाजगाम लुब्धस्तदानीं मृगलिप्सुरुग्रः।
en: Having controlled all his senses, speech, and mind Krishna laid himself down in high Yoga. A fierce hunter of the name of Jara then came there, for finding a deer.

sa: तस्याश्रुपरिपूर्णाक्षो व्यूढोरस्को महाभुजः। आर्तस्यार्ततरः पार्थः पादौ जग्राह भारत॥
en: The broad-chested and mighty-armed son of Pritha, more afflicted than his uncle with his eyes bathed in tears, touched his uncle's feet, O Bharata.

sa: तस्य मूर्धानमाघ्रातुमियेषानकदुन्दुभिः। स्वस्रीयस्य महाबाहुर्न शशाक च शत्रुहन्॥
en: The mighty-armed Anakadundubhi wished to smell the head of his sister's son, but could not do it, O destroyer of enemies.

sa: सर्वथा वृष्णिदारास्तु बालं वृद्धं तथैव च। नयिष्ये परिगृह्याहमिन्द्रप्रस्थमरिंदम॥
en: I shall, however, O chastiser of enemies, first remove to Indraprastha the women of the Vrishni race as also the children and the aged.'

sa: अलुप्तधर्मस्तं धर्मं कारयित्वा स फाल्गुनः। जगाम वृष्णयो यत्र विनष्टा भरतर्षभ।॥
en: Phalguna, who was careful in observing every duty having caused this duty to be performed, went. O chief of Bharata's race, next to the place where the Vrishnis were killed.

sa: बहूनि च सहस्राणि प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च। भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकस्त्रीणां हतनाथानि निर्ययुः॥
en: The widows of the other heroes of the Bhoja, the Vrishni and the Andhaka races, lordless now, that started with Arjuna, numbered many millions.

sa: नकुलः पतितस्तस्मादागच्छ त्वं वृकोदर। यस्य यद् विहितं वीर सोऽवश्यं तदुपाश्नुते॥
en: It is for this that Nakula has fallen down. Know this, O Vrikodara! That O hero, which has been ordained for a person, must have to be borne by him.'

sa: अयं श्वा भक्त इत्येवं त्यक्तो देवरथस्त्वया। तस्मात् स्वर्गे न ते तुल्यः कश्चिदस्ति नराधिपः॥
en: On the present occasion, thinking the dog to be devoted to you, you have renounced the very car of the celestials instead of renouncing him. Hence, O king, there is not one in Heaven that is equal to you.

sa: अत्र स्नातस्य भावस्ते मानुषो विगमिष्यति। गतशोका निरायासो मुक्तवैरो भविष्यसि॥
en: Having bathed in this river, you will be divested of your human nature. Indeed, your grief dispelled, your ailments conquered, you will be freed from all enmities.

sa: हतास्तस्मिन् महायुद्धे ये वीरास्तु महारथाः। घटोत्कचादयश्चैव देवान् यक्षांश्च भेजिरे॥
en: Those heroic and powerful car-warriors, viz., Ghatotkacha and others, who were killed in the great battle, attained to the status, some of celestials and some of Yakshas.

sa: अह्ना यदेनः कुरुते इन्द्रियैर्मनसापि वा। महाभारतमाख्याय पश्चात् संध्यां प्रमुच्यते॥
en: The sins that one commits during the day by one's senses or the mind are all washed off before evening by reciting a portion of the Mahabharata.

sa: ईदृशाद् वाचकाद् राजश्रुत्वा भारत भारतम्। नियमस्थः शुचिः श्रोता शृण्वन् स फलमश्नुते॥
en: Listening to the Bharata, O king, when recited, O you of Bharata's race, by a reader of this kind, listener, observant of vows the while and purified by purificatory rites, acquires valuable fruits.

sa: अप्सरोगणसंकीर्णं विमानं लभते महत्। प्रहृष्टः स तु देवैश्च दिवं याति समाहितः॥
en: He acquires a large (celestial) car full of various orders of Apsaras. With a glad heart and with celestials in his company, he proceeds to the celestial region, his heart rapt (in felicity).

sa: अलङ्कारं प्रदद्याच्च पाण्योर्वे भरतर्षभ। कर्णस्याभरणं दद्याद् धनं चैव विशेषतः॥
en: Ornaments, O chief of Bharata's race for the arms as also those for the ears, should be given. Besides these other kinds of riches should be presented.

sa: अजीवनाहेण मया नृशंसा कृता प्रतिज्ञा नियमेन तावत्। त्वया हि बाल्यात् प्रतिपन्नमेतत् तन्मा दहेद् वेणुमिवात्मपुष्पम्॥
en: My sands run out; by me has this cruel promise been made with an oath. But this (exile of Sītä) has been thought of by you through your ignorance. Let it not, however, consume you like a bamboo flower destroying the bamboo.

sa: एतदत्स्यसि मद्धस्तान्न त्वां वाधिष्यते शुभे। क्षुधा तृषा च रम्भोरु वर्षाणामयुतैरपि॥
en: If you partake of these from my hand, you shall never O beauteous one, be afflicted either with hunger or thirst, O you of thighs resembling rambhā (trunks), for years.

sa: देवलिङ्गानि दृष्टानि रामलक्ष्मणसंनिधौ। तानि दर्शय देवेन्द्र यदि त्वं देवराट् स्वयम्॥
en: By the side of Rāma and Lakşmaņa, I had beheld the signs of the celestials. If, O Devendra, you are yourself the sovereign of the celestials, show those to me.

sa: तवाज्ञया च देवेन्द्र पयोभूतमिदं हविः। अशिष्यामि त्वया दत्तं रघूणां कुलवर्घनम्॥
en: And by your command, O Devendra, will I partake of this pāyasa cooked with milk, which has been offered to me, and which shall enhance (the prosperity) of our race.

sa: गतप्रभा द्यौरिव भास्करं विना व्यपेतनक्षत्रगणेव शर्वरी। पुरी बभासे रहिता महात्मना कण्ठास्रकण्ठाकुलमार्गचत्वरा ॥
en: And with her terraces overflowing with tears that flooded the throats of the mourners, the city appeared like the welkin without its splendour in the absence of the sun, or the night with the stars enveloped.

sa: सीते विमुच्यतामेषा वनवासकृता मतिः। बहुदोषं हि कान्तारं वनमित्यभिधीयते॥
en: Renounce therefore, Oh Sītă, your intention of flying as an exile to the forest, which for its impenetrableness is said to abound in evils.

sa: सग्राहाः सरितश्चैव पङ्कवत्यस्तु दुस्तराः। मत्तैरपि गजैर्नित्यमतो दुःखतरं वनम् ॥
en: The rivers are full of crocodiles, sharks, and other fearful animals, muddy and impassable and always infested with infuriated elephants; so the wood is full of misery.

sa: उपहारश्च कर्तव्यः कुसुमैः स्वयमाहतैः। आर्षेण विधिना वेद्यां सीते दुःखमतो वनम्॥
en: One has to offer presents of flowers collected by his ownself to the altars, O Sītā, according to the rites of the ascetics; so the wood is full of misery.

sa: तस्मिन्युगे प्रज्वलिते ब्रह्मभूते त्वनावृते॥ अमृत्यवस्तदा सर्वे जज्ञिरे दीर्घदर्शिनः।
en: And for this, the Brāhmaṇas were the highest caste, effulgent in asceticism, asceticism, shorn shorn of ignorance, above death and conversant with three ages.

sa: आमिषं यच्च पूर्वेषां राजसं च मलं भृशम्। अनृतं नाम तद्भूतं क्षिप्तेन पृथिवीतले॥ अनृतं पातयित्वा तु पादमेकमधर्मतः। ततः प्रादुष्कृतं पूर्वमायुषः परिनिष्ठितम्॥
en: And for houses and farms that were the property of the former age, people of the Tretā Yuga were possessed by envy, the outcome of the quality of darkness. And with the treading of impiety on earth during Tretā, the soiled sin of untruth appeared. And this iniquity stretching one footstep, the lease of people's lives, for sins, became limited.

sa: मृगपक्षिगणाश्चैव सिद्धाश्रमनिवासिनः। अनुजग्मुर्महात्मानं विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम्॥
en: And birds and beasts dwelling in Siddhāśrama followed the high-souled Viśvāmitra having asceticism for wealth.

sa: रामोऽप्युत्थाप्प राजानं कैकेय्याभिप्रचोदितः। कशयेव हतो वाजी वनं गन्तुं कृतत्वरः॥
en: Raising the king up, Rāma, being directed by Kaikeyī, began to hurry on his departure to the forest, like to a steed struck sharp with a whip.

sa: पर्याप्तोऽहं गदापाणिर्हन्तुं प्राणान् रणे तव। त्रयाणामपि लोकानां पाशहस्त इवान्तकः॥
en: I can, mace in hand, deprive you and the three worlds to boot clean of your lives, like the very Destroyer with the noose in his hand.

sa: शरीरं मृगरूपस्य विनिर्भिद्य शरोत्तमः॥ मारीचस्यैव हृदयं बिभेदाशनिसंनिभः।
en: And that best of arrows, like to a thunderbolt, deeply pierced the breast of Mārīca, wearing the shape of a deer.

sa: बाढमित्येव सौमित्रिः कृत्वा राघवशासनम्। प्राद्रवद्रथमारुह्य राघवस्य निवेशनम्॥
en: Thereupon being apprised of Rāghava's command and saying 'so be it.' Saumitri ascended his car and went speedily towards Rāma's abode.

sa: सुखोषिताः स्म भगवंस्त्वया पूज्येन पूजिताः। आपृच्छामः प्रयास्यामो मुनयस्त्वरयन्ति नः॥
en: O Reverend sir, we we have stayed here pleasantly, being excellently ministered to by you. We greet you, and go away. The ascetics urge speed upon us.

sa: न तं वध्यमहं मन्ये सर्वैर्देवासुरैरपि। अयं तस्य वधोपायस्तन्ममैकमनाः शृणु॥
en: I deem him incapable of being slain by all the Gods and Asuras together. This alone is the means of slaying. Do you heedfully listen to it!

sa: अरोचयत तद्वाक्यं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः। चिन्तयित्वा महाबाहुरकम्पनमुवाच ह॥
en: Thereupon, the lord of the Rākṣasas, Rāvaņa, happened to relish those words; and reflecting (a while), that mighty-armed one addressed Akampana.

sa: चपला ह्यविनाताश्च चलचित्ताश्च वानराः। न सहिष्यन्ति ते नादं सिंहनादमिव द्विषा:॥
en: And volatile and haughty and of fickle minds, the monkeys will not be able to bear your shouts; even as elephants are incapable of bearing the roaring of a lion.

sa: विद्वते च बले तस्मिन्रामः सौमित्रिणा सह। अवशस्तु निरालम्बः प्रहस्तवशमेष्यति॥
en: And on that monkey-army running away, Rāma in company with Sumitrās son, deprived of his power and shorn of support, shall, O Prahasta, come under your subjection.

sa: सा बभूव मुहूर्तेन भीमैर्नानाविधायुधैः॥ लङ्का राक्षसवीरैस्तैर्गजैरिव समाकुला। हुताशनं तर्पयतां ब्राह्मणांश्च नमस्यताम्॥ आज्यगन्धप्रतिवहः सुरभिर्मारुतो ववौ।
en: In a moment Lankā swarmed with heroic and terrific Rākşasas equipped with various arms, as if with elephants, as well as with people worshipping Fire and bowing down to Brāhmaṇas. And the perfumed breeze blew, laden with the incense of sacrificial offerings.

sa: अहं ह्याजिस्थितस्यास्य करिष्यामि यदीप्सितम्। वृक्षैर्मुष्टिप्रहारैश्च पीडितः प्रतियास्यति ॥
en: I shall deal with him mercifully in the battle as you does wish and being struck with fists and trees he shall fly away.

sa: मुक्तस्तु वज्रनिर्घोषः प्रदीप्ताशनिसंनिभः। राघवेण महाबाणो वालिवक्षसि पातितः॥
en: And a mighty shaft, like to thunderbolt and resembling flaming fire, being hurled by Rāma, alighted on the breast of Väli.

sa: नरोत्तमः कालयुगान्तकोपमं शरोत्तमं काञ्चनरूपभाषितम्। ससर्ज दीप्तं तममित्रमर्दनं सधूममग्निं मुखतो यथा हरः॥
en: As the great God Hara emitted forth fire with smoke from his mouth, so that best of men like to Death hurled an excellent, flaming and foedestroying shaft, resembling gold and death itself.

sa: धृष्टिर्जयन्तो विजयः सुराष्ट्रो राष्ट्रवर्धनः। अकोपो धर्मपालश्च सुमन्त्रश्चाष्टमोऽर्थवित्॥
en: They were, Dhrsti, Jayanta, and Vijaya, and Surăştra, and Răstravardhana, and Akopa and Dharmapala, and Sumantra the cight, conversant with profit.

sa: भर्तृजेन तु दुःखेन अभिभूता वनौकसः। शिरांस्यभिहनिष्यन्ति तलैर्मुष्टिभिरेव च॥ सान्त्वेनानुप्रदानेन मानेन च यशस्विना। लालिता: कपिनाथेन प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यन्ति वानराः॥
en: The dwellers of the woods overwhelmed with grief got of (the decease of) their master, shall strike at their heads with their clenched fists and hands. And the monkeys affectionately cherished by the famous lord of the monkeys with soothing words gifts and regard, shall resign there lives.

sa: तापसो वा भविष्यामि नियतो वृक्षमूलिकः। नेतः प्रतिगमिष्यामि तामदृष्ट्वासितेक्षणाम्।।४३
en: Or restraining myself, I shall become an ascetic living underneath trees; but return I will not, without obtaining a sight of that dark-eyed damsel.

sa: जित्वा तु राक्षसान् देवीमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दिनीम्। सम्प्रदास्यामि रामाय सिद्धीमिव तपस्विने॥
en: Having vanquished the Rākşas, I will bestow on Rāma the lady of the Ikşvāku race like the fruit of asceticism conferred on an ascetic.

sa: लक्ष्मणस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा शत्रुनिबर्हणः। वृत्रघातमशेषेण कथयेत्याह सुव्रत॥
en: Hearing the words of Laksmana, Rama, the slayer of enemies, said:-0 you of firm vows, do you at length, describe the destruction of Vrtra.

sa: तं महोरगसंकाशं प्रगृह्य परिघं रणे। दूषणोऽभ्यपतद् रामं क्रूरकर्मा निशाचरः॥
en: And taking up in that encounter the parigha (an iron club) resembling a mighty snake, that ranger of the night of cruel deeds Duşaņa, rushed towards Rāina.

sa: भ्रष्टस्तस्य महाकायः पपात रणमूर्धनि। परिघश्छिन्नहस्तस्य शक्रध्वज इवाग्रतः॥
en: And the huge parigha (an iron club) escaping from (Dusana's grasp) fell forward on the field like the banner of Sakra.

sa: तस्य सैन्यस्य सर्वस्य खरः शेषो महारथः। राक्षसस्त्रिशिराश्चैव रामश्च रिपुसूदनः॥
en: And the remnant of his (Khara's) forces were that mighty car-warrior, Khara himself, and the Raksasa, Trisirā; and (on the other side) was that destroyer of foes-Rāma.

sa: मार्गमाणस्तु वैदेहीं सीतामायतलोचनाम्। सर्वतः परिचक्राम हनूमानरिसूदनः॥
en: Searching for Videha's daughter, the large eyed Sītā, that slayer of enemies, Hanumān, ranged all through (this edifice).

sa: तासां संवृतदान्तानि मीलिताक्षीणि मारुतिः। अपश्यत् पद्मगन्धीनि वदनानि सुयोषिताम्॥
en: And the Wind-god's offspring beheld the countenance of those beauteous women, with closed eyes, having their lashes shut through languor; and odorous with lotus-perfume.

sa: युद्धकामेन ताः सर्वा रावणेन हृताः स्त्रियः। समदा मदनेनैव मोहिताः काश्चिदागताः॥
en: And all those women had been procured by Rāvana because he sought fight (with their relations) and some haughty dames, rapt with desire, had of themselves come to this place.

sa: रामेत्युक्त्वा तु वचनं वाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणः। शशाक नृपतिर्दीनो नेक्षितुं नाभिभाषितुम्॥
en: Uttering the word "Rāma" only, the poor king with his eyes full of tears could not see him nor could he speak to him.

sa: प्रियं त्वामप्रियं वक्तुं वाणी नास्य प्रवर्तते। तदवश्यं त्वया कार्यं यदनेनाश्रुतं मम॥
en: You are his most beloved son and word does not proceed from his mouth to speak you things unpleasant. But it behoves you to carry out what the monarch has promised to me.

sa: तस्याभूत्सुमहांस्त्रासः कुत्सा चात्मन्यजायत। लङ्कां प्रदहता कमें किंस्वित्कृतमिदं मया॥
en: And worked up with fear and remorse, he reflected, “What a mighty iniquity have I perpetrated by burning down Lankā of my own accord.

sa: तयोः सुचरितं स्वार्थं शाठ्यात् परिजिहीर्षतोः। यदि नैवं व्यवसितं स्याद्धि प्रागेव राघव। ययौ प्रागेव दत्तश्च स्याद् वरः प्रकृतश्च सः॥ लोकविद्विष्टमारब्धं त्वदन्यस्याभिषेचनम्। नोत्सहे सहितुं वीर तत्र मे क्षन्तुमर्हसि ॥
en: With a desire to renounce you by fraud, they simulate piety which is but selfishness. Had they not purposed thus, Oh, Rāghava, things would not have taken such a turn. If this story of the vows be true, then why had it not been declared before Surely has the monarch engaged in an action hateful to the people, namely the installation of a younger brother neglecting you (the eldest one). Pray, pardon me, oh great hero, I cannot brook all this.

sa: तां दृष्ट्वा हनुमान् सीतां मृगशावनिभेक्षणाम्। मृगकन्यामिव त्रस्तां वीक्षमाणां समन्ततः॥ दहन्तीमिव निःश्वासैर्वृक्षान् पल्लवधारिणः। संघातमिव शोकानां दुःखस्योर्मिमिमिवोत्थिताम्॥ तां क्षामां सुविभक्ताङ्गी विनाभरणशोभिनीम्। प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे मारुतिः प्रेक्ष्य मैथिलीम्॥
en: And Sītā, of dark-blue eyes, was protected by virtue of her own character. And beholding Sītā, having the eyes of a young antelope, and terrified and casting her looks hither and thither like a hind and burning down the trees enveloped with leaves by her breath; like to a mass of grief and an upheaval of sorrow; having well-proportioned limbs, and appearing graceful without ornaments, Maruti attained to an excess of delight.

sa: ते क्षिप्रमभिगम्याथ यूथपा यूथपर्षभम्। हरयो वानरश्रेष्ठं परिवार्योपतस्थिरे॥
en: Thereupon proceeding quickly the commanders of various monkey herds stood encircling the king of monkeys and the chief of · leaders.

sa: यस्मादुद्विग्नचेतास्त्वं विद्रुतो हरिपुङ्गव। तं क्रूरदर्शनं क्रूरं नेह पश्यामि वालिनम्॥
en: I do not behold, O best of monkeys, that wicked Vāli of terrible looks, afraid of whom you had fled away and for whom you are anxious.

sa: वालिप्रणिहितावेव शङ्केऽहं पुरुषोत्तमौ। राजानो बहुमित्राश्च विश्वासो नात्र हि क्षमः॥
en: Methinks these two best of men have been despatched by Vali. Kings have many friends. And it is not proper for me to place confidence in them.

sa: नमस्कुरुष्व कौन्तेय तस्मै शान्ताय वै सदा॥ रुद्राय शितिकण्ठाय कनिष्ठाय सुवर्चसे।
en: O son of Kunti, bow down to him who is peace incarnate, to him called Rudra (of the fierce), who is of blue throat, exceedingly subtle and of great effulgence.

sa: सहस्रशिरसे चैव सहस्रनयनाय च॥ सहस्रबाहवे चैव सहस्रचरणाय च।
en: To him who has a thousand heads; him who has a thousand eyes; and him who has a thousand arms and a thousand legs.

sa: पुनश्च संदधे दीप्तान् देवानां निशिताशरान्॥ सधूमान् सस्फुलिङ्गांश्च विद्युत्तोयदसंनिभान्।
en: Once more Mahadeva aimed ai the gods a shower of burning and sharp resembling tongues of fire mixed with smoke or clouds with lightning.

sa: आरुह्य स रथं दिव्यं सर्वदेवमयं शिवः॥ त्रिपुरस्य वधार्थाय स्थाणुः प्रहरतां वरः। असुराणामन्तकरः श्रीमानतुलविक्रमः॥ स्तूयमानः सुरैः पार्थ ऋषिभिश्च तपोधनैः।
en: The god Siva, riding on that wonderful car composed of all the excellent celestial forces proceeded for the destruction of the tripple city. Indeed Sthanu, that foremost of Smiters, that destroyer of Asuras, that most beautifullooking warrior of infinite energy, adored by the gods and Rishis, possessed of the wealth of asceticism, O Partha.

sa: वेदे चास्य समाम्नातं शतरुद्रियमुत्तमम्। नाम्ना चानन्तरुद्रेति ह्युपस्थानं महात्मनः॥
en: In the Vedas, the excellent hymn called Shatarudriya has been sung in his praise, he who is the great Lord called the infinite Rudra.

sa: ज्येष्ठं भूतं वदन्त्येनं ब्राह्मणा मुनयस्तथा। प्रथमो ह्येष देवानां मुखादस्यानलोऽभवत्॥
en: The Brahmanas and the sages call him the most ancient of beings. He is the first-born of all the gods and fire came out from his mouth.

sa: तैजसी महती दीप्ता देवेभ्योऽस्य शिवा तनुः। भास्वती मानुषेष्वस्य तनु?राग्निरुच्यते॥
en: His auspicious form surcharged with energy is more blazing than all the forms of the other gods. Amongst men his blazing and dreadful form is called Fire.

sa: धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं पुण्यं वेदैश्च सम्मितम्। देवदेवस्य ते पार्थ व्याख्यातं शतरुद्रियम्॥
en: O Partha, thus the hymn approved of Vedas and called Sata-rudriya in honour of that god of gods has been explained to thee which is excellent glorious, life-enhancing and sacred.

sa: कच्चिद् राजर्षिवंशोऽयं त्वामासाद्य महीपतिम्॥ यथोचितं महाराज यशसा नावसीदति। इत्येवंवादिनं तं स न्यायवित् प्रत्यभाषत॥
en: Are the ladies of your households duly honoured in your house, O best of men? I hope, O king. that this race of royal sages, having to you for their king, have not fallen away from fame and glory?

sa: यष्टा क्रतुसहस्राणां दाता दानपतिः प्रभुः। ययातिः सर्वकाशीश इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥
en: The performer of a thousand sacrifices and the lord who, in gifts, was the prince of givers, Yayati, the ruler of all the Kashis said these words,

sa: अतीत्य च नृपानन्यानादित्यकुलसम्भवान्। मत्सकाशमनुप्राप्तावेतां बुद्धिमवेक्ष्य च॥
en: And especial considering that they had come to him passing over the kings born in the solar race.

sa: विरमेच्छुष्कवैरेभ्यः कण्ठायासांश्च वर्जयेत्। यथा वैतंसिको युक्तो द्विजानां सदृशस्वनः॥ तान् द्विजान् कुरुते वश्यांस्तथा युक्तो महीपतिः। वशं चोपनयेच्छन् निहन्याच्च पुरंदर॥
en: One should avoid useless acts of hostility as also insolent speech. As a fowler, carefully uttering cries like those of the birds he wishes to catch, or destroy, captures and brings them under his control, even so should a king, O Purandara, bring his enemies under subjection and then kill them if he likes.

sa: खद्योतैरिव संयुक्तमन्तरिक्षं व्यराजत। रुक्मपृष्ठानि चापानि व्यतिषिक्तानि धन्विनाम्॥ पततां लोकवीराणां सव्यदक्षिणमस्यताम्। रथा रथैः समाजग्मुः पादातैश्च पदातयः॥
en: The sky shone resplendent as if with (a number of) fire-flies. Changing their bows feathered in gold from one hand to another, the heroes began to smite each other discharging their shafts right and left. The charioteers fought with charioteers, the infantry fought with infantry.

sa: तच्छ्रुत्वा माता सरमा तत्सत्रमुपागच्छत्, यत्र स जनमेजयः सह भ्रातृभिर्दीर्घसत्रमुपास्ते॥
en: Hearing this her mother, being very sorry for the affliction of his son, went to the place where Janamejaya with his brothers were attending his long sacrifice.

sa: एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच-'एतत् प्रत्यनुनये भवन्तावश्विनौ, नोत्सहेऽहमनिवेद्य गुरवेऽपूपमुपयोक्तुम्' इति॥
en: Thus addressed he said, "O Ashvinis, I ask your pardon. I cannot take this cake without offering it to my preceptor.

sa: साधयामस्तावदित्युक्त्वा प्रातिष्ठतोत्तंङ्कस्ते कुण्डले गृहीत्वा। सोऽपश्यदथ पथि नग्नं क्षपणकमागच्छन्तं मुहुर्मुहुर्दृश्यमानं च॥
en: Uttanka, having said this, went away with the ear-rings. On his way he saw a naked beggar, coming towards him. He was sometimes coming in view view and sometimes disappearing.

sa: कार्यकालं हि मन्येऽहं विधिदृष्टस्य कर्मणः। तद्गच्छापचिति राजन्पितुस्तस्य महात्मनः॥
en: The time has come, I say, for your taking vengeance, ordained by Fate. Go, O king and revenge the death of your noble father,

sa: कबन्धशतसंकीर्णं छत्रचामरसंकुलम्। सेनावनं तच्छुशुभे वनं पुष्पाचितं यथा॥
en: Covered with hundreds of headless trunks and strewn with umbrellas and yakyails, that vast army looked beautiful like a blossoming forest.

sa: श्रुत्वैव तु महाशब्दं धृष्टद्युम्नशिखण्डीनौ। धर्मराजं पुरस्कृत्य मद्रराजमभिद्रुतौ॥
en: On hearing that loud sound Dhristadyumna and Shikhandin, placing king Yudhishthira at their head, rushed against the king of the Madras.

sa: सा कम्पमाना मोहेन बाहुभ्यामसितेक्षणा। वृत्ताभ्यामनुरूपाभ्यामूरू समवलम्बत॥
en: Trembling with faintness, the black-eyed lady supported her with her thighs and with her plump and becoming arms.

sa: सर्वत:पाणिपादश्च सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखः। सर्वत:श्रुतिमाँल्लोके सर्वं व्याप्य स तिष्ठति॥
en: It has hands and feet on every side. It has ears on every side. It pervades every thing in the universe.

sa: हैडिम्बाश्च महावीर्यो विहगो मद्बलोपमः। वहेदनघ सर्वान्नो वचनात् ते घटोत्कचः॥
en: O sinless one, at your command, the son of Hidimba, Ghatotkacha, who can range the skies and who is as strong as myself will carry us all.

sa: उत्थानवीरः पुरुषो वाग्वीरानधितिष्ठति। उत्थानवीरान् वाग्वीरा रमयन्त उपासते॥
en: The hero who works is superior to one who speaks. The heroes who speak, gratify and worship the heroes who work.

sa: एकाङ्गेनापि सम्भूतः शत्रुर्दुर्गमुपाश्रितः। सर्वं तापयते देशमपि राज्ञः समृद्धिनः॥
en: With only one kind of force, an enemy, from within a fort, can assail the whole country of even a powerful and prosperous king.

sa: मृगपक्षिगणाश्चैव पृतनां बहुशस्तव। अपसव्यं तदा चक्रुर्वेदयन्तो महाभयम्॥
en: A large number of animals and birds, kept to the right of your army and emitted noise foreboding a dreadful calamity.

sa: संजय उवाच इति बहु परुषं प्रभाषति प्रमनसि मद्रपती रिपुस्तवम्। भृशमभिरुषितः परंतपः कुरुपृतनापतिराह मद्रपम्॥
en: Sanjaya said When the king of Madra was thus, in all sincerity, addressing these harsh words to him and singing the glories of his enemy, that slayer of foes, the commander of the Kuru army, excited with anger, said.

sa: गङ्गायाः सुरनद्या स्वादु भूत्वा यथोदकम्। महोदधेर्गुणाभ्यासाल्लवणत्वं निगच्छति॥
en: Even as the very tasteful water of the celestial river Ganga flowing into that of the mighty main, aitains saline properties.

sa: इरावांस्तु ततो राजन्ननुविन्दस्य सायकैः। चतुरभिश्चतुरो वाहाननयद् यमसादनम्॥
en: Then in that conflict, Iravat, O king's with four arrows, dispatched the four steeds of Anuvinda to the regions of Death.

sa: तौ स जित्वा महाराज नागराजसुतासुतः। पौरुषं ख्यापयंस्तूर्णं व्यधमत् तव वाहिनीम्॥
en: Obtaining victory, O monarch, over the two brothers, the son of the daughter of the king of the Nagas displaying his inanliness, began speedily to spread havoc among your soldiers.

sa: तत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वा ऋषयश्च समागताः। विशेषं न स्म विविदुईडिम्बभगदत्तयोः॥
en: Then there came the celestial along with the Gandharvas and the sages. They were unable to find out any destruction between the son of Hidimba and Bhagadatta.

sa: भैमसेनि रथस्थं तु तत्रापश्याम भारत। शेषा विमनसो भूत्वा प्राद्रवन्त महारथाः॥
en: We then only beheld the son of Bhimasena (Ghatotkacha), O Bharata riding on his car the rest of the car-warriors, with minds distracted (with fear) had fled (in all directions.

sa: निहत्य ताशरान् राजा राक्षसस्य धनुश्च्युतान्। भैमसेनि रणे तूर्णं सर्वमर्मस्वताडयत्॥
en: Then king Bhagadatta, severing those arrows shot from the bow of the Rakshasas, in that combat quickly pierced the son of Bhimasena in all his vital parts.

sa: स्वस्त्रीयाभ्यां नरव्याघ्रो नाकम्पत यथाऽचलः। प्रहसन्निव तां चापि शस्त्रवृष्टिं जघान ह॥
en: Shot by his nephews, that foremost of men (the Madra king) moved not, but stood still even like a mountain; then as if smiling, he baffled that shower of arrows.

sa: स शरः प्रेषितस्तेन गरुडानिलवेगवान्। मद्रराजं विनिर्भिद्य निपपात महीतले॥
en: That dare shot by him and coursing swiftly like the Garuda himself, penetrating through the body of the Madra king, fell down on earth.

sa: रौक्मिणेयश्च साम्बश्च युयुधानश्च सात्यकिः। सुधर्मा चानिरुद्धश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः॥
en: Namely, the son of Rukmani (Pradyumna), Samba, Yuyudhana, the son of Satyaka (Satyaki), Sudharmana, Anirudha, Shaivya, these foremost of men (all waited upon Yudhishthira).

sa: तत्र भारत भीमेन नाराजाभिहता गजाः। पेतुर्नेदुश्च सेदुश्च दिसश्च परिबभ्रमुः॥
en: There, in that battle, O Bharata, many were the elephants that pierced with Nacharas by Bhima, fell and were confounded and shrieked and careered in all directions.

sa: छिन्नहस्ता महानागाश्छिन्नगात्राश्च मारिष। क्रौञ्चवद् व्यनदन् भीताः पृथिवीमधिशेरते॥
en: Huge elephants, with their trucks cut off, and their bodies mangled, fell down on the earth, O sire, screaming like cranes.

sa: अनुकषैः शुभै राजन् योक्त्रैश्चैव सरश्मिभिः। संकीर्णा वसुधा भाति वसन्ते कुसुमैरिव॥
en: With well-made car-bottoms, and O king, with reins and riggings-covered with all these things, the earth appeared as beautiful as she appears during the spring being strewn over with blossoms.

sa: महापापानि कर्माणि यानि केवलसाहसात्। आरभ्यन्ते भीमसेन व्यथन्ते तानि भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, O Bhimasena, the greatly sinful deeds that one wants to perforin depending only on his courage become a source of pain to him.

sa: ततस्तु क्षत्रियाः केचिज्जामदग्न्यभयार्दिताः। विविशुर्गिरिदुर्गाणि मृगाः सिंहार्दिता इव॥
en: Then, some of the Kshatriyas, stricken with the terror of Jamadagni's son, entered mountain fastnesses, like deer afflicted by the lion.

sa: अलं द्यूतेन गान्धारे विदुरो न प्रशंसति। न ह्यसौ सुमहाबुद्धिरहितं नो वदिष्यति॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O son of Gandhara, there is no need of playing dice. Vidura does not praise it. That greatly intelligent man will never give me advice that is not good for me.

sa: ज्येष्ठोऽयमिति मां मत्वा श्रेष्ठश्चेति विशाम्पते। युधिष्ठिरेण सत्कृत्य युक्तो रत्नपरिग्रहे॥
en: O king, on consideration of my being the eldest and the foremost. I was engaged in receiving the gems and jewels (brought as tribute by the kings).

sa: उपस्थितानां रत्नानां श्रेष्ठानामर्घहारिणाम्। नादृश्यत परः पारो नापरस्तत्र भारत॥
en: O descendant of Bharata, the limit and the like of the excellent and the invaluable jewels that were brought there have never been seen.

sa: अथ शप्तश्च भगवान् गौतमेन पुरन्दरः। अहल्यां कामयानो वै धर्मार्थं च न हिंसितः॥
en: The illustrious Purandara, an account of his having coveted the body of Ahalya, was cursed by Gautama, yet for the sake of Virtue and wealth, the Rishi did not destroy outright the king of the celestials.

sa: विप्रेषु ददतश्चैव श्रद्धा भवतु नित्यशः। अनन्यासु सवर्णासु पुत्रजन्म च मे भवेत्॥
en: I desire also the boon, that everyday I may give away devoutly my wealth to the Brahmanas. I wish also to beget sons upon females of my own order and not upon others.

sa: अन्नं मे ददतः श्रद्धा धर्मे मे रमतां मनः। अविनं चास्तु मे नित्यं धर्मकार्येषु पावक॥
en: Let devotion be the ruling feeling of my heart when I shall give away edibles; let also my mind delight in the fountain of righteousness. Let, O Agni, no difficulty overtake me when I engage myself in the performance of pious deeds."

sa: नक्षत्रेषु च सर्वेषु ददनक्षत्रदक्षिणा:। ईजे च विविधैर्यज्ञैर्यथा सोमोऽङ्गिरा यथा॥
en: Under every (auspicious) conjunction of the constellations, he gave away presents specified for those occasions. Verily the monarch performed various sacrifices like another Soma or another Angirasa.

sa: जनक उवाच अक्षरक्षरयोरेष द्वयोः सम्बन्ध इष्यते। स्त्रीपुंसोऽपि भगवन् सम्बन्धस्तद्वदुच्यते॥
en: Janaka said O holy one, it has been said that the relation between male and female is like that which exists between the Indestructible and the Destructible.

sa: तस्मात् त्वं शृणु राजेन्द्र यथैतदनुदृश्यते। याथातथ्ये सांख्येषु योगेषु च महात्मसु॥
en: Listen now to me, O king, as to how the subject of Liberation has been explained among the great persons conversant with the Sankhya and the Yoga Systems of Philosophy.

sa: धृतराष्ट्र उवाच भगवन्नेवमेवैतद् यथा वदसि नारद। इच्छामि चाहमप्येवं न त्वीशो भगवन्नहम्॥
en: Dhritarashtra said O you endued with divine prosperity, it is as you say O Narada, and I too wish the same thing, but you endued with heavenly prosperity, I am not the master.

sa: त्वयापि प्रतिपत्तव्यं तथैव भरतर्षभ। स्वेषु बन्धुषु मुख्येषु मा मन्युवशमन्वगाः॥
en: By you too should they be treated in the same way, O you best among the race of Bharata; do not show anger towards your own kinsmen.

sa: अस्तु शेषं कौरवाणां मा पराभूदिदं कुलम्। कुलन इति नोच्येथा नष्टकीर्तिनराधिप॥
en: Let not this race of Kurus be exterminated ard let not yourself be spoken of as the destroyer of the race and be of great notoriety, O lord of men.

sa: विषयेषु च संसर्गाच्छाश्वतस्य च दर्शनात्। मनसा चान्यदाकाङ्क्षन् परं न प्रतिपद्यते॥
en: On account of attachment to worldly objects, in view of the joys of the highest heaven, and for seeking something other than Brahma, men do not attain to the Supremc.

sa: जिह्माक्षाः प्रललाटाश्च निर्मांसहनवोऽपि च। वज्रबाहङ्गुलीचक्राः कृशा धमनिसंतताः॥ प्रविशन्ति च वेगेन साम्पराये छुपस्थिते। वारणा इव सम्मत्तास्ते भवन्ति दुरासदाः॥
en: Those, who have crooked eyes, and broad foreheads, and check-bones not fleshy, and arms strong as thunderbolts, and fingers bearing circular marks, and who are sparely built, and whose arteries and nerves are visible, rush with great impetuosity when the collision of battle takes place. Resembling angry elephants, they become irresistible.

sa: अधार्मिका भिन्नवृत्ताः सान्त्वेनैषां पराभवः। एवमेव प्रकुप्यन्ति राज्ञोऽप्येते ह्यभीक्ष्णशः॥
en: Of wicked conduct and foreign manners, they consider soft speeches as marks of defeat. If treated leniently, they always show anger against their sovereign.

sa: भीष्म उवाच परतन्त्रं कथं हेतुमात्मानमनुपश्यसि। कर्मणां हि महाभाग सूक्ष्मं ह्येतदतान्द्रियम्॥
en: Bhishma said Why, O fortunate one, do you regard your soul, which is dependent, to be the cause of your deeds? Its inaction is subtle and imperceptible to the senses.

sa: काल उवाच न ह्यहं नाप्ययं मृत्यु यं लुब्धक पन्नगः। किल्बिषी जन्तुमरणे न वयं हि प्रयोजकाः॥
en: Kala said Neither Mrityu, nor this serpent, nor I, O fowler, am guilty of the death of any creature. We are merely the immediate causes of the event. O Arjunaka, the Karma of this child was the exciting cause of our action in this matter.

sa: तपसा महता युक्तं प्रदास्यति महाद्युते। स्त्रियौ त कारणं तत्र परिवर्ते भविष्यतः॥
en: The illustrious Richika will grant this son to your race, this Kshatriya who will be endued with high penances. Two women will be the cause in the matter of this exchange of sons.

sa: एवमेतद् भवेद् राजन् कार्यापेक्षमनन्तरम्। यदभिप्रेतमन्यत् ते ब्रूहि यावद् ब्रवीम्यहम्॥
en: Thus, O monarch, (their superiority or inferiority) depends on their utility. Now if you have anything more to ask, speak out and I shall solve your doubts.

sa: विराटो द्रुपदश्चैव माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ॥ दुद्रुवुर्भीष्ममेवाजौ रक्षिता दृढधन्वना।
en: Virata and Draupada, the two sons of Madri begotten by Pandu, all rushed against Bhishma, their attack being covered by the firm bowman Arjuna.

sa: ते सर्वे दृढधन्वानः संयुगेष्वपलायिनः॥ बहुधा भीष्ममानछुर्मार्गणैः क्षतमार्गणैः।
en: All those firm bowmen, never receding from the fight pierced Bhishma on many parts of his body with arrows steadily directed.

sa: ततो निद्रावशं प्राप्तौ कृपभोजौ महारथौ। सुखोचितावदुःखार्ही निषण्णौ धरणीतले॥
en: The two great car-warriors, Kripa and Kritavarman, began to sleep. They ever deserving of happiness and undeserving of misery, slept on the bare ground.

sa: वृकोदरेण क्षुद्रेण सुनृशंसमिदं कृतम्। मूर्धाभिषिक्तस्य शिरः पादेन परिमृद्नता॥
en: Another wicked act has been perpetrated by the mean Vrikodara for the latter has touched with his foot the head of a crowned person.

sa: सद्भिः पुरस्तादभिपूजित: स्यात् सद्भिस्तथा पृष्ठतो रक्षितः स्यात्। सदासतामतिवादांस्तितिक्षेत् सतां वृत्तं चाददीतार्यवृत्तः॥
en: You should always keep the virtuous man before you as your model. You should always compare your acts with those of the virtuous. You should always disregard the cruel words of the wicked.

sa: स्थानीकं नरव्याघ्राः केचिदभ्यपतन रथैः। अभज्यन्त युगैरेव युगानि भरतर्षभ॥
en: O foremost of men, some warriors attacked with their cars the cars of the enemies, and crushed the yokes of those cars to pieces.

sa: अश्वैरच्यजवैः केचिदाप्लुत्य महतो स्थान्। शिरांस्याददिरे वीरा रथिनामश्वसादिनः॥
en: Some heroic horsemen on fleet steeds leaped up and cut off the heads of car-warriors who were seated on their cars.

sa: साश्वारोहान् विषाणाप्रैक्षिप्य तुरगान् गजाः। रथौघानभिमृद्नन्तः सध्वजानभिचक्रमुः॥
en: Overthrowing with their tusks steeds and their riders, some elephants roved about and crushed cars with their standards.

sa: अप्रधृष्यमजेयं च देवदानवराक्षसैः। भेत्तारं गिरिशृङ्गाणां समुद्रजलशोषणम्॥
en: Incapable of being overcome by the Devas and Danavas, capable of splitting mountains and of sucking the ocean,

sa: तं पर्वतं महाकुक्षिमुद्दिश्य स महाखगः! जवेनाभ्यपतत्तार्क्ष्य: सशाखागजकच्छपः॥
en: The great bird, carrying the bough, the elephant and the tortoise, proceeded in great speed towards that mountain of broad waist.

sa: शाखिनो बहवश्चापि शाखायाऽभिहतास्तया। काञ्चनैः कुसुमैर्भान्त विद्युत्त्वन्त इवाम्बुदाः॥
en: The falling bough struck down many trees, which, with golden flowers amid their dark leaves, looked like clouds charged with lightning.

sa: समर्थो बलिना श्रेष्ठो हर्तुं सोमं विहंगमः। सर्वं संभवायाम्यस्मिन्नसाध्यमपि साधयेत्॥
en: And the strongest of all the strong, that bird is capable of taking away the Soma. Everything is possible in him. He can achieve even the unachievable.

sa: चक्राणि परिघांश्चैव त्रिशूलानि परश्वधान्। शक्तीश्च विविधास्तीक्ष्णा: करवालांश्च निर्मलान्। स्वदेहरूपाण्यादाय गदाश्चोग्रप्रदर्शनाः॥
en: They were armed with many discusses, iron maces, spikes, lances, tridents, battle-axes and various other sharp-pointed missiles, polished swords and maces of terrible forms, all suited to their respective bodies.

sa: एते राजर्षयः पुण्याः कीर्तिमन्तो बहुश्रुताः। तस्यां सभायां राजेन्द्र वैवस्वतमुपासते॥
en: O king of kings, these holly royal sages, all of great achievements and great knowledge of the Shastras, waited upon the of Vaivasvata, (Yama) in that assembly-hall.

sa: चित्राङ्गदाचित्रमाल्याः सर्वे ज्वलितकुण्डलाः। सुकृतैः कर्मभिः पुण्यैः पारिबहेच भूषिताः॥
en: All adorned in bracelets and garlands, with ear-rings of burnished gold, and with their own holy acts and with the marks of their orders.

sa: भीष्म उवाच चेदिराजकुले जातस्त्र्यक्ष एष चतुर्भुजः। रासभारावसदृशं ररास च ननाद च॥
en: Bhishma said This Shishupala was born with three eyes and four hands in the dynasty of the kings of Chedi. As soon as he was born, he screamed and brayed like an ass.

sa: एष ते नृपतेः पुत्रः श्रीमाञ्जातो बलाधिकः। तस्मादस्मान्न भेतव्यमव्यगः पाहि वै शिशुम्॥
en: The Voice said. O king, this your son, who has been (just) born, will become fortunate and superior in strength. Therefore you have no fear from him. Cherish this child without (any) anxiety.

sa: संश्रुत्योदाहृतं वाक्यं भूतमन्तर्हितं ततः। पुत्रस्नेहाभिसंतप्ता जननी वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥
en: Bhishma said. Having heard these words, the mother becoming anxious by affection for her son, spoke thus to the invisible being.

sa: अभिवाद्य यथान्यायं यथाश्रेष्ठं नृपं च ताम्। कुशलानामयं पृष्ट्वा निषण्णौ रामकेशवौ।॥
en: Saluting every body according to his rank and saluting also the king and the queen and inquiring after every body's welfare, Rama and Keshava (Balaram and Krishna) took their seats.

sa: यथाक्रमेण भगवंस्तीर्थानामनुपूर्वशः। ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मविदां श्रेष्ठ परं कौतूहलं हि मे॥
en: Tell me these, in their order, O illustrious man. My curiosity is not to be satisfied, O foremost of all persons conversant with the knowledge of Brahman.

sa: ततः सोमे ओषध्यो न प्रजज्ञिरे॥ निरास्वादरसाः सर्वा हतवीर्याश्च सर्वशः।
en: On account, of the wasting of Soma the deciduous herbs failed to grow, Their juices dried up they became tasteless and all of them lost their virtues.

sa: तौ दृष्ट्वा समरे विनिघ्नन्तौ परस्परम्। दुर्योधनानुजाः सर्वे शूराः संत्यक्तजीविताः॥
en: Beholding those two enraged heroes strike one another in battle, the younger brothers of Duryodhana, all of whom were ready to lay down lives their in battle.

sa: निर्जित्य समरे द्रोणं कृतिनं चित्रयोधिनम्। यथा पशुगणान् सिंहस्तद्धद्धन्ता सुतान् मम॥
en: Like a lion slaying other inferior beasts Satyaki is slaughtering my sons, having first vanquished in battle Drona that warrior accomplished in weapons and versed in all modes of warfare.

sa: ब्राह्मण उवाच नैतदस्ति पृथग्भाव: किंचिदन्यत् ततः सुखम्। नैतदस्त्यपृथग्भावः किंचिद् दुःखतरं ततः॥
en: The Brahmana said There exists nothing that is separate from it. There is nothing more delightful than it. There is nothing that is un-separated from it. There is nothing more afflicting than it.

sa: नदीनां सङ्गमश्चैव वैताने समुपह्वरे। स्वात्मतृप्ता यतो यान्ति साक्षादेव पितामहम्॥
en: And there is a confluence also of rivers in the secluded spot for sacrifice. Thence those who are contented with their own souls proceed to the Grandfather.

sa: राम उवाच भीष्म कां बुद्धिमास्थाय काशिराजसुता तदा। अकामेन त्वयाऽऽनीता पुनश्चैव विसर्जिता॥
en: Rama said I Bhishma, in what frame of mind was the daughter of the king of Kashis led away by you though you wanted her not; and why was she again sent away.

sa: स्वधर्मं पुरुषव्याघ्र राजपुत्री लभत्वियम्। न युक्तस्त्ववमानोऽयं राज्ञां कर्तुं त्वयानघ॥
en: Let this princess fulfill her object, О best among men, and it is not proper, O king, that she should be disgraced by you, O sinless one.

sa: यस्यान्नेनावशेषेण जठरे यो म्रियेद् द्विजः। तां तां योनि व्रजेद् विप्रो यस्यान्नमुपजीवति॥
en: The Brahmana in his next life comes by the position of that order upon whose food he lives through life or with the undigested portion of whose food in his stomach he dies.

sa: एते योनिफला देवि स्थानभागनिदर्शकाः। स्वयं च वरदेनोक्ता ब्रह्मणा सृजता प्रजाः॥
en: The boongiving Brahman, while he created all creatures, himself said that the division of human beings into the four orders as dependant on birth is only for purposes of classification.

sa: गच्छ राजानमासाद्य स्वकर्म कथयस्व वै। अदत्तादानमेवं हि कृतं पार्थिवसत्तम॥
en: Go to the king confess what you have done. Tell him,-O best of kings, I have committed the offence of taking what was not given to me.

sa: श्रीमहेश्वर उवाच हन्त तेऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि देवि कर्मफलोदयम्। मर्त्यलोके नरः सर्वो येन स्वफलमश्नुते॥
en: The God of Gods said Indeed, O goddess, I shall describe to you the fruits of acts. It is by them that all human beings in this world enjoy or suffer the consequences of their acts.

sa: सर्वमेतदतिक्रम्य श्रुत्वा परमतं भवान्। यत् प्राप्तकालं मन्येथास्ततं कुर्याः पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: Shutting your mind to all this and hearing what the intentions of the enemy are, do that what you consider to be opportune, O foremost among men.

sa: निवृत्तवनवासान् नः श्रुत्वा वीर समागताः। अक्षौहिण्यो हि सप्तेमास्त्वत्प्रसादाज्जनार्दन॥
en: Hearing that, we are returned from our exile in the woods, O hero. These seven Akshauhinis have gathered round us through your grace, OJanardana.

sa: अकाम इव तं राजा गणयस्वेत्युवाच ह। एकदेशं च शाखायाः समादिष्टं मयानघ॥ गणयस्वाश्वतत्त्वज्ञ ततस्त्वं प्रीतिमावह। सोऽवतीर्य रथात् तूर्णं शातयामास तं दुमम्॥
en: Surely the king most unwillingly said to him count. (He also said), “O unblameable one, O you versed in the knowledge of horses, having counted (the leaves and fruits of) one portion of this branch, you will be satisfied of the truth of my affirmation." He (Nala) then dismounted from the car with all haste and cut down the tree.

sa: ततो जयन्त्यां राजेन्द्र सोमतीर्थं समाविशेत्॥ स्नात्वा फलमवाप्नोति राजसूयस्य मानवः।
en: O king of kings, one should then go to the Soma Tirtha, situated in Jayanti, Bathing in it a man obtains the fruits of the Rajasuya sacrifice.

sa: यच्च रोषाभिभूतेन क्षत्रमुत्सादितं त्वया। ततश्च पापान्मुक्तस्त्वं पतितास्ते स्वकर्मभिः॥
en: You have exterminated the Kashtriyas from wrath, but you are already freed from that sin, for they have fallen for their own (mis) deeds.

sa: कपिलातीर्थमासाद्य ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः। तत्र स्नात्वार्चयित्वा च पितृन् स्वान् दैवतान्यपि॥ कपिलानां सहस्रस्य फलं विन्दति मानवः।
en: Leading the life of a Brahmachari and having one's soul subdued, he who goes to the Tirtha, called Kapila and bathes in it and worships the Pitris and the celestials, that man, obtains the fruit of giving away one thousand Kapila kine.

sa: ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र द्वारपालमरन्तुकम्। तच्च तीर्थं सरस्वत्यां यक्षेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः॥ तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन्नग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्।
en: O king of kings, one should then go to the gatc-keeper, Arantuka, which is in the Sarasvati and which belongs to the illustrious chief of the Yakshas (Kubera). O king, bathing one in it, a man obtains the fruits of Agnishtoma (sacrifice).

sa: तत्र स्नात्वार्चयित्वा च शूलपाणिं वृषध्वजम्। सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा गच्छेत परमां गतिम्॥
en: Bathing in it and worshipping there the wielder of trident, Vrishadhvaja (Shiva), one obtains the highest state, all his sins being destroyed and his soul being purified.

sa: ततो व्यासवनं गच्छेत्रियतो नियताशनः। मनोजवे नरः स्नात्वा गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्॥
en: One should then go with regulated diet and subdued soul to Vyasavana. Bathing there in the Mancjava one obtains the fruits of giving away one thousand kine.

sa: ब्रह्मादिभिः सुरै राजऋषिभिश्च तपोधनैः। विज्ञप्तो वै महादेव ऋषेरथ नराधिप॥
en: O ruler of men, O king, then Brahma and other celestials and the ascetic Rishis all went to Mahadeva and represented to him all about the Rishi.

sa: ततो गच्छेतधर्मज्ञ तीर्थं संनिहतीमपि॥
en: O virtuous one, one should then go to the Tirtha called Sannihati.

sa: चक्रे वसुस्ततः पूजां विष्वक्सेनाय भारत। जप्यं जगौ च सततं नारायणमुखोद्गतम्॥
en: Then Vasu, O Bharata, began to worship the Creator of the universe and to recite silently those sacred Mantras that had come out of Narayana's mouth in days of yore.

sa: वयांसि पशवश्चैव भूतानि च जनाधिप। गृहस्थैरेव धार्यन्ते तस्माच्छेरूष्ठो गृहाश्रमी॥
en: Birds and animals and various other creatures, O king, supported by a are householders. He, therefore, who belongs to that mode of life, is superior to all.

sa: स मया मूढया पुत्रो ज्ञायमानोऽप्युपेक्षितः। तन्मां दहति विप्रर्षे यथा सुविदितं तव॥
en: Foolish that I am, although he knew me for his mother when he grew up, yet I did not try to acknowledge him. This burns me, O Rishi, as is well-known to you.

sa: ध्रुवो जयः पाण्डवानामितीदं न संशयः कश्चन विद्यतेऽत्र। जयध्वयो दृश्यते पाण्डवस्य समुच्छ्रितो वानरराज उग्रः॥
en: The sure success of the Pandavas will follow in this case, there is no doubt of it; the fierce triumphal banner, of the son of Pandu who has the figure of the monkey on his banner, is already hoisted.

sa: मिन्द्रात्मजं द्रोणमुखा विमः। कृपश्च शल्यश्च विविंशतिश्च दुर्योधनः सौमदत्तिश्च राजन्॥
en: O king, thus against that son of Indra who was like Indra himself rushed many warriors headed by Drona, Kripa, Shalya, Vivingshati, Duryodhana and also Somadatta's son.

sa: तथैव भीष्माहतमन्तरिक्ष महास्त्रजालं कपिराजकेतोः। विशीर्यमाणं ददृशुस्त्वदीया दिवाकरेणेव तमोऽभिभूतम्॥
en: Your troops then saw that shower of arrow, shot by that great ape-bannered hero, opposed and dispersed by Bhishma, as the sun dispels darkness.

sa: कथ्यमानं मया तात त्वं हि मेऽर्धं स्मृतः पुरा। नमोऽतियशसे तस्मै देहिनां परमात्मने॥
en: As I recite them to you. It is said that in days of yore you formed half my body. Salutations to Him of great glory. Him, viz., that is the Supreme Soul of all embodied creatures.

sa: तस्मिन्काले तु जपतस्तस्य वीरस्य धीमतः। नादेयं ब्राह्मणेष्वासीत्किंचिदृसु महीतले॥
en: When he was thus engaged in his worship, there was nothing on earth that the heroic and intelligent Vasusena would not give to Brahmanas.

sa: कुर्वाणश्चोत्तमं कर्म कर्णः पार्थजिगीषया॥ व्यंसनेनाश्वसेनस्य पन्नगेन्द्रस्य वै पुनः।
en: Karna had done a great feat for defeating Partha. You frustrated the object of Ashvasena, the son of that prince of snakes (viz., Takshaka).

sa: न च वो हृदि कर्तव्यं यदयं घातितो रिपुः। मिथ्यावध्यास्तथोपायैर्बहवः शत्रवोऽधिकाः॥
en: Ye should not mind that this enemy of yours has been killed deceitfully. When the number of one's enemics becomes great, then destruction should be brought about by wily ways.

sa: पाञ्चालपुत्रस्त्वरितस्तु शूरो गदां प्रगृह्याचलशृङ्गकल्पाम्। ससम्भ्रमं भारत शत्रुघाती जवेन वीरोऽनुससार नागम्॥
en: Then, taking up his mace resembling the crest of a mountain, the brave Panchalas appeared there. Fearlessly, O king, that hero, that striker of foes, rushed quickly against the clephant.

sa: तथा दैत्यगणान् सर्वान् यक्षगन्धर्वराक्षसान्। नागानप्सरसश्चैव विद्धि मत्प्रभवान् द्विज॥
en: So also, O twice-born one, know that all the tribes of the Daityas, all the Yakshas, Gandharvas, Rakshasas, Nagas, Apsaras, have originated from me.

sa: दुःशासनेन यत् कृष्ण एकवस्त्रा रजस्वलाः। परिक्लिष्टा सभामध्ये सर्वलोकस्य पश्यतः॥
en: Clad in onc piece of cloth and in her scason, the princess Krishna was treated cruelly by Dushasana in the midst of the assembly and before all.

sa: न च ते व्यसनैर्योक्तुं शक्या दिष्टकृतेन च। शकिताश्चेप्सवश्चैव पितृपैतामहं पदम्॥
en: They are aided by Fate. When they are desirous of regaining the place of their fathers and grandfathers, we can never succeed to injure them by any means of ours.

sa: वैशम्पायन उवाच इत्युक्त्वा तं चिताग्निस्थं धर्मपत्नी नरर्षभम्। मद्रराजसुता तूर्णमन्वारोहद् यशस्विनी॥
en: Vaishampayana said : Having said this, the daughter of the king of Madra, the lawfully wedded wife of that best of men Pandu, ascended the funeral pyre of her lord.

sa: कृष्णेन वाक्यमुक्तोऽसि सुहृदां शममिच्छता। अन्वपद्यस्व तत् तात मा मन्युवशमन्वगाः॥
en: “By Krishna has been spoken the words of a friend wishing for peace; listen to that my dear son, and do not follow the lead if vindictiveness.

sa: अनुतिष्ठ महाप्राज्ञ कृष्णभीष्मौ यदूचतुः। माधवं बुद्धिमोहेन माऽवमंस्थाः परंतप॥
en: Follow, O greatly wise man, what the two, Krishna and Bhishma have said; do not from perverted understanding insult Madhava, O chastiser of foes.

sa: युधिष्ठिस्यास्मि निदेशकारी पार्थस्तृतीयो युधि संस्थितोऽस्मि। तदर्थमावृत्य मुखं प्रयच्छ नरेन्द्रवृत्तं स्मर धार्तराष्ट्र॥
en: I am the obedient servant of Yudhishthira. I am the third son of Pritha, standing here for battle. Turning back, show me your face. Remember the conduct of kings, O son of Dhritarashtra.

sa: युधिष्ठिर उवाच उद्यता यज्ञभागा हि साक्षात् प्राप्ताः सुरैरिह। किमर्थमिह न प्राप्तो दर्शनं स हरिविभुः॥
en: Yudhishthira said In the great sacrifice of Uparichara, all the gods appeared in their respective forms for partaking of the sacrificial offerings and were seen by all. Why is it that the powerful Hari only acted otherwise by invisibly taking his share?

sa: मेरोरुत्तरभागे तु क्षीरोदस्यानुकूलतः। स देशो यत्र नस्तप्तं तपः परमदारुणम्॥
en: The country where we practised these austerest of penances, lies to the north of the mountains of Meru and on the shores of the ocean of milk.

sa: न च पश्याम पुरुषं तत्तेजोहृतदर्शनाः। ततो नः प्रादुरभवद् विज्ञानं देवयोगजम्॥
en: At this, the idea, due to the grace of the great God Himself, sprung in our minds that one who had not practised sufficient penances could not soon see Narayana.

sa: देव उवाच दृष्टा वः पुरुषाः श्वेताः सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जिताः॥ दृष्टो भवति देवेश एभिर्दृष्टैद्विजोत्तमैः।
en: These white men, who are divested of all external senses, competent to see (Narayana). Only those foremost of twice-born persons whom these white men honoured with their looks, can see the great God.

sa: उपायं कर्मसिद्धौ च भगवन् वक्तुमर्हसि। निवारयेयं येनेन्द्रं वर्षमाणं महावने॥
en: O illustrious one, you should give us the means by which we may gain success; and we can prevent Indra from pouring rains on that extensive forest.

sa: राजोवाच ब्रवीतु भगवान् समयमिति॥
en: The king said: O exalted one, tell me what was your pledge.

sa: पुरोहिताः शत्रुवधं वदन्तो ब्रह्मर्षिसिद्धाः श्रुतवन्त एनम्। जप्यैश्च मन्त्रैश्च महौषधीभिः समन्ततः स्वस्त्ययनं ब्रुवन्तः॥
en: Many priests, Brahmanas, Rishis, Siddhas, as they walked round him, chanted hymns in his praise. They wished him the destruction of his enemies by the help of Tapas and mantras, efficacious drugs and various propitiatory ceremonies.

sa: अथ यज्ञविभूतिं तां काङ्क्षसे भरतर्षभ। ऋत्विजस्तव तन्वन्तु सप्ततन्तुं महाध्वरम्॥
en: O best of the Bharata race, if you desire to possess the dignity of performing a sacrifice, let Ritvijas arrange for you the great sacrifice, called Saptatantu.

sa: कृतवैरः पुरा चैव सहदेवेन मारिष। योत्स्यते सततं राजंस्तवार्थं कुरुनन्दन॥
en: My child, in former days, he was made an enemy by Sahadeva, and he will ever fight on your behalf, O you delighter of the Kuru race.

sa: युद्धाभिकामौ समरे क्रीडन्ताविव यूथपौ। यूथमध्ये महाराज विचरन्तौ कृतान्तवत्॥
en: Desirous of war they will act in battle each like Yama like two sporting elephants moving in the midst of a herd, O king.

sa: स गत्वा पाण्डवान् सर्वानुवाचाभिप्रणम्य च। दुर्योधनो महाराज यजते नृपसत्तमः॥ स्ववीयर्जितमर्थौघमवाप्य कुरुसत्तमः। तत्र गच्छन्ति राजानो ब्राह्मणाश्च ततस्ततः॥
en: Thereupon he went there and bowing down his head to all the Pandavas said "O great king, the foremost of kings that Veda of the Kurus, Duryodhana is performing a sacrifice after having acquired immense wealth by his own prowess. Brahmanas from all quarters are going to it.

sa: अथ पुरोहितो राजानमब्रवीत्। प्राणरक्षार्थं श्येनाद् भीतो भवन्तं प्राणार्थी प्रपद्यते॥
en: Thereupon the priest thus spoke to the king," Afraid of the hawk, this pigeon has come to you for his life with the intention of saving it.

sa: योऽष्टमासांस्तु शुचिना किरणेनोक्षितं पयः। प्रत्यादत्ते पुनः काले किमाश्चर्यमतः परम्॥
en: What can be more wonderful than this that drinking up for eight months the rain he pours down he pours it down again in the rainy season.

sa: प्रजज्ञे राक्षसी पुत्रं भीमसंनान्महाबलम्। विरूपाक्षं महावक्त्रं शरूकर्णं विभीषणम्॥
en: She then gave birth by Bhima a greatly strong son of terrible eyes and large mouth, of ears like arrows and of appearance fearful.

sa: मुनिदेशात् परश्चैव प्रोच्यते दुन्दुभिस्वनः। सिद्धचारणसंकीर्णो गौरप्रायो जनाधिप॥
en: Next to Munidesha is Dundubhisvana frequented by the Siddhas and the Charanas. O king, the people of this regions are white.

sa: एते देशा महाराज देवगन्धर्वसेविताः। पुष्करे पुष्करो नाम पर्वतो मणिरत्नवान्॥
en: O king, all these countries are inhabited by the celestial and the Gandharvas. In Pushkara (island) there is a mountain called Pushkara, full of gems and jewels.

sa: परिणाहेन षट्त्रिंशद् विपुलत्वेन चानघ॥ पष्टिमाहुः शतान्यस्य बुधाः पौराणिकास्तथा।
en: And because because it is very large, its circumference is forty two thousand Yojanas. O sinless one, thus say the learned men of old.

sa: अहंकारो न कर्तव्यो याज्ये तस्मिन् नराधिपे। स्थातव्यं च वशे तस्य स ते छेत्स्यति संशयम्॥
en: Although the king of Mithila is one in whose sacrifices we officiate, still you should not indulge in any feeling of superiority while living with him. You should live under his direction and in obedience to him. He will remove your doubts.

sa: तस्या द्वारं समासाद्य निःशङ्कः प्रविवेश हा तापि द्वारपालास्तमुग्रवाचा न्यषेधयन्॥
en: Arrived at the gate, he sent word through the guards, he reached the king's palace and entered it without any-hesitation. The gatekeepers prevented him with harsh words.

sa: ततस्तेषां गुणानेव कीर्तयामि विशेषतः। नावबुध्येत विदुरो ममाभिप्रायमिङ्गितैः॥
en: Therefore, I was highly applauding them, (the Pandavas), so that Vidura may not know my real desire even by a sign.

sa: ततस्तु मद्राधिपतिर्महात्मा युधिष्ठिरं भीमबलं प्रसह्या विव्याध वीरं हृदयेऽतिवेगं शरेण सूर्याग्निसमप्रभेण॥
en: Displaying his vigor, then the illustrious king of the Madras struck the heroic Yudhishthira of terrible might in the chest with an arrow effulgent like the fire or the sun.

sa: अथास्य चर्माप्रतिमं न्यकृन्त भीमो महात्मा नवभिः पृषत्कैः। खड्गं च भल्लैर्निचकर्त मुष्टौ नदन् प्रहृष्टस्तव सैन्यमध्ये॥
en: Then the illustrious Bhima cut off the ten arrows the matchless shield of that hero. With another broad-headed arrow he cut off the sword also of that warrior. Filled with joy at this, he cried aloud in the midst of the army.

sa: दीप्तामथैनां प्रहितां बलेन सविस्फुलिङ्गां सहसा पतन्तीम्। प्रेक्षन्त सर्वे कुरवः समेता दिवो युगान्ते महतीमिवोल्काम्॥
en: All the Kauravas beheld that blazing dart sending forth scintillations of fire as it passed through the sky after having been discharged with great force, like a large meteor dropping from the sky at the end of the cycle.

sa: शक्त्या विभिन्नह्रदयं विप्रविद्धायुधध्वजम्॥ संशान्तमपि मद्रेशं लक्ष्मी व विमुञ्चति।
en: Though deprived of his weapons and standard and though his heart had been cut and slain still his body was not shorn of beauty.

sa: शल्यानुजं हतं दृष्ट्वा तावकास्त्यक्तजीविताः॥ वित्रेसुः पाण्डवभयाद् रजोध्वस्तास्तदा भृशम्।
en: Beholding Shalya's younger brother killed your troops, hopeless of their lives; were pursued by the fear of the Pandavas and fled, coated with dust.

sa: चापमार्गबलोद्धतान् मार्गणान् वृष्णिसिंहयोः॥ आकाशगानपश्याम पतङ्गानिव शीघ्रगान्।
en: The arrows of those two Vrishni chiefs, shot off their bows, appeared like swiftlycoursing insects in the sky.

sa: तन्निकृत्तं धनुः श्रेष्ठमपास्य शिनिपुङ्गवः॥ अन्यदादत्त वेगेन वेगवत्तरमायुधम्।
en: Casting off his bow which was thus cut off, that heroe, quickly took up another that was stronger than the first.

sa: अश्वत्थामा ततो राज्ञा हताश्वं विरथीकृतम्। तमपोवाह हार्दिक्यं स्वरथेन युधिष्ठिरात्॥
en: Then Ashvatthaman, taking upon his car, the son of Hridika who had been deprived of his horses by the (Pandava) king, took him away from Yudhishthira's presence.

sa: रथप्रवरमास्थाय नरो नारायणानुगः। विधुन्वन् गाण्डिवं संख्ये बभौ सूर्य इवोदितः॥
en: Riding on his own best of chariots, the embodied Nara accompanied by Narayana, shaking his Gandiva bow in battle appeared shining and dazzling like the risen sun.

sa: गन्धर्वाप्सरसाकीर्णे नानादुमलतावृते। ऋषिसङ्घः परिवृतं दक्षं धर्मभृतां वरम्॥ पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे च ये च स्वर्लोकवासिनः। सर्वे प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा उपतस्थुः प्रजापतिम्॥
en: Over-grown with trees and creepers of various sorts, that place abounded with Gandharvas and Apsaras. Sorrounded by numbers of Rishis, Daksha, that best of virtuous men, that progenitor of creatures, was attended by the denizens of the Earth, the sky, and the celestial region, with their hands joined together in respect.

sa: दधीचिरुवाच सर्वेषामेव मन्त्रोऽयं येनासौ न निमन्त्रितः। यथाहं शंकरादूर्ध्वं नान्यं पश्यामि दैवतम्। तथा दक्षस्य विपुलो यज्ञोऽयं न भविष्यति॥
en: Dadhichi said This seems to be the advice of all that are here, namely, that Maheshvara should not be invited. As, however, I do not see any god that can be said to be superior to him, I am sure that this proposed Sacrifice of Daksha will surely be destroyed. a

sa: जानुभ्यामवनीं गत्वा दक्षो लब्ध्वा भवाद् वरम्। नाम्नामष्टसहस्रेण स्तुतवान् वृषभध्वजम्॥
en: Having gained that boon from Bhava, Daksha knelt down to him and adored that god having the bull for his emblem uttering his thousand and eight names.

sa: अनेनैव तु देहेन गणानां समतां व्रजेत्। तेजसा यशसा चैव युक्तो भवति निर्मलः॥
en: By listening or reciting this hymn, one, even in this earthly body of his, acquires equality with the spirits who are the attendants of Mahadeva. One gains energy and fame, and becomes purged of all sin.

sa: कश्यपस्य द्विजातेश्च कथं वै पक्षिराट् सुतः। अधृष्यः सर्वभूतानामवध्यश्चाभवत्कथम्॥
en: Why had Kashyapa, a Brahmana, the king of the birds for his son? Why was he invincible of all creatures and indestructible of all?

sa: इन्द्राच्छतगुणः शौर्ये वीर्ये चैव मनोजवः। तपसो नः फलेनाद्य दारुणः संभवत्विति॥
en: By the fruit of our penances, let there be born a hero, who is hundred times stronger and valorous than Indra, fleet as the mind and frightful to present Indra."

sa: ब्राह्मण उवाच अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्। सुभगे पञ्चहोतृणां विधानमिह यादृशम्॥
en: The Brahmana said Regarding it, О blessed lady, is cited the ancient story of what kind the institution is of the five sacrificing priests.

sa: परस्य दण्डं नोद्यच्छेत् क्रद्धो नैनं निपातयेत्। अन्यत्र पुत्राच्छिष्याच्च शिक्षार्थं ताडनं स्मृतम्॥
en: One should not angrily, take up the rod of punishment for laying it upon another. Only the son or the pupil, it has been said, can be mildly reprimanded for purposes of instruction.

sa: कृत्वा मूत्रपुरीषे तु रथ्यामाक्रम्य वा पुनः। पादप्रक्षालनं कुर्यात् स्वाध्याये भोजने तथा॥
en: Having answered calls of nature or having walked over a road, one should wash his feet. One should also wash his feet before sitting to recite the Vedas or to eat any food.

sa: द्विजच्छेदं न कुर्वीत भुक्त्वा न च समाचरेत्। महाकुले प्रसूतां च प्रशस्ता लक्षणैस्तथा॥ वयःस्थां च महाप्राज्ञः कन्यामावोढुमर्हति। अपत्यमुत्पाद्य ततः प्रतिष्ठाप्य कुलं तथा॥ पुत्राः प्रदेया ज्ञानेषु कुलधर्मेषु भारत। कन्या चोत्पाद्य दातव्या कुलपुत्राय धीमते॥
en: One should not kill a bird (for eating it), especially after having fed it, A wise man should espouse a maiden born in a high family, gifted with auspicious marks, and of full age. Begetting children upon her and thus perpetuating his race by that means, one should make over his sons to a good preceptor for being educated generally, O Bharata, as also in the especial customs of the family, O monarch. The daughters that one may beget should be married to youths of respectable families, who are again possessed of intelligence.

sa: प्राङ्मुख: श्मश्रुकर्माणि कारयेत् सुसमाहितः। उदङ्मुखो वा राजेन्द्र तथायुर्विन्दते महत्॥
en: One should sit facing either the east or the north while being shaved by a barber. By so doing, O great king, one succeeds in living long.

sa: पत्नी रजस्वला या च नाभिगच्छन्न चाह्वयेत्॥ स्नातां चतुर्थे दिवसे रात्रौ गच्छेद् विचक्षणः।
en: When one's wife is in her season, one should never know her, nor even summon her for conversation. A wise man may take her into his company on the fourth day after the bath of purification.

sa: हस्तिपृष्ठेऽश्वपृष्ठे च रथचर्यासु चैव ह॥ यत्नवान् भव राजेन्द्र यत्नवान् सुखमेधते।
en: Do then, O king, carefully attend to the practice of riding an elephant, a horse and a warchariot. The man who attends to these with care, succeeds in acquiring happiness.

sa: अज्ञानात् परिपृच्छामि त्वं हि ज्ञानमयोनिधिः। तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि सर्वमेतदसंशयम्॥
en: I am ignorant while you are an Ocean of knowledge. Hence, I ask you. Verily, I wish to hear you describe all these subject.

sa: ततोऽहं लघुभिश्चित्रैरस्त्रैस्तानसुरान् रणे। चिच्छेद सायुधान् राजन् शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः॥
en: O king, then, in the fight, I cut off the Danavas by hundreds and thousands who were furnished with arms, by various swift weapons.

sa: ईर्यमाणेन सततं ब्रह्मघोषेण सर्वशः। ब्रह्मलोकसमं पुण्यमासीद् द्वैतवनं सरः॥
en: Resounding always and all over with the recitations of the Veda, the lake of the forest became as holy as the region of Brahma.

sa: सुपूरा वै कुनदिका सुपूरो मूषिकाञ्जलिः। सुसंतोषः कापुरुषः स्वल्पकेनैव तुष्यति॥
en: Bad (small) rivers are filled with a handful water and douses are satisfied with little and a coward is ever well satisfied, for a little satisfies him.

sa: अलब्वा यदि वा लब्ध्वा नानुशोचति पण्डितः। आनन्तर्यं चारभते न प्राणानां धनायते॥
en: A wise man grieves not whether he is successful or not in his object; on the contrary he commences what ought to be done under the altered circumstances without caring for his life.

sa: उद्यम्य धुरमुत्कर्षेदाजानेयकृतं स्मरन्। कुरु सत्त्वं च मानं च विद्धि पौरुषमात्मनः॥
en: Remembering the exertion made by horses of good breed in moving heavy weight know what in your own manliness lies and bring together all you sense of honour and energy.

sa: मातोवाच किमद्यकानां ये लोका द्विषन्तस्तानवाप्नुयुः। ये त्वादृतात्मनां लोकाः सुहृदस्तान् ब्रजन्तु नः॥
en: The mother said The world which is (reserved) for the poor and miserable, may our enemies attain to; and may our well-wishers roam about in the earth which is (reserved) for respected souls.

sa: यमाजीवन्ति पुरुषं सर्वभूतानि संजय। पक्वं दुममिवासाद्य तस्य जीवितमर्थवत्॥
en: The man, depending on whom all living creatures depend, O Sanjaya as (birds) on a tree with ripe fruits, has his life rendered useful.

sa: ततस्तं नृपशार्दूलं शार्दूलसमविक्रमम्। आरोहयद्धयं तूर्णं भ्राता दुःशासनस्तदा॥ अङ्गदी बद्धमुकुटो हस्ताभरणवान् नृप। धार्तराष्ट्रो महाराज विबभौ स पथि व्रजन्॥
en: Accompanied by his brothers, and loO king like Indra surrounded by the celestial. Thereafter, his brother Dushasana, helped that foremost of kings equal to a tiger in strength, to mount on his steed. Decked with bracelets, with a diadem on his head, and O king, his arms graced with other ornaments,

sa: अभिवाद्य ततो भीष्मं निषण्णः परमासने। काञ्चने सर्वतोभद्रे स्पास्तरणसंवृते॥
en: And then descending from his horse, that ruler of men approached Bhishma. Thereafter doing obeisance to Bhishma, he seated himself on a beautiful seat,

sa: उत्सहेम रणे जेतुं सेन्द्रानपि सुरासुरान्। किमु पाण्डुसुतान् वीरान् ससुहृद्गणबान्धवान्॥
en: "Reliving upon you, O slayer of foes, we are even capable of vanquishing in battle the celestials and the Asuras united together, with Indra at their head,

sa: तस्मादर्हसि गाङ्गेय कृपां कर्तुं मयि प्रभो। जहि पाण्डुसुतान् वीरान् महेन्द्र इव दानवान्॥
en: What to speak of the sons of Pandu though they may be warlike and supported by their friends, allies and kinsmen. Therefore, O son of Ganga, O lord, it behold you to be merciful on me.

sa: अनुजानीहि समरे कर्णमाहवशोभिनम्। स जेष्यति रणे पार्थान् ससुहृद्गणबान्धवान्॥
en: For my unfortunate self, you are inclined to spare the sons of Pandu, then permit Karna, that ornament of battle, to join the fight.

sa: न तत्रासीत् पुमान् कश्चित् पाण्डवानां विशाम्पते। अन्यत्र रथिनां श्रेष्ठाद् भीमसेनान्महाबलात्॥
en: Not a single person of the Pandava host remained there on the field of battle, except, O ruler of men that foremost of car-warriors namely Bhimasena endued with great prowess.

sa: अपराजितो महाराज पराजिष्णुर्महारथम्। शरैर्बहुभिरान द् भीमसेनं महाबलम्॥
en: That conqueror of foes, namely Aparajita himself, O mighty monarch, that mighty carwarrior, pierced the highly powerful Bhimasena, with innumerable shafts.

sa: निहता भ्रातरः शूरा भीमसेनेन मे युधि। यतमानास्तथान्येऽपि हन्यन्ते सर्वसैनिकाः॥
en: “My heroic brothers have all been slain in battle by Bhimasena; and other soldiers, through striving their best of resist him, are all being slain and slaughtered.

sa: शिपिविष्टेति चाख्यायां हीनरोमा च यो भवेत्। तेनाविष्टं तु यत्किचिच्छिपिविष्टेति च स्मृतः॥
en: Shipivishta is a name. The word Shipi means a person who has no hair on his body. He who pervades all things in the form of Shipi passes by the name of Shipivishta.

sa: यास्को मामृषिरव्यग्रो नैकयज्ञेषु गीतवान्। शिपिविष्ट इति ह्यस्माद् गुह्यनामधरो ह्यहम्॥
en: The Rishi Yashka, with quiet soul, in many a sacrifice invoked me by the name Shipvishta. It is therefore that I came to bear this secret name.

sa: त्रयो हि धातवः ख्याताः कर्मजा इति मे स्मृताः। पित्तं श्लेष्मा च वायुश्च एष संघात उच्यते॥ एतैश्च धार्यते जन्तुरेतैः क्षीणैश्च क्षीयते। आयुर्वेदविदस्तस्मात् त्रिधातुं मां प्रचक्षते॥
en: There are three well-known ingredients of the body. They have their origin in action, and are called Bile, Phlegm, and Wind. The body is called a union of these three. All living creatures are kept up by these three, and when these three become weakened, living creatures also become weakened. It is, therefore, that all persons well-versed in the scriptures of the science of Life call me by the name of Tridhatu.

sa: तच्छूलं भस्मसात्कृत्वा दक्षयज्ञं सविस्तरम्॥ आवयोः सहसागच्छद् बदर्याश्रममन्तिकात्।
en: That dart, having consumed all the articles of Daksha's sacrifice, came with great force towards us at the retreat of Badari.

sa: निष्प्रभाणि च तेजांसि ब्रह्मा चैवासनच्युतः॥ अगाच्छोषं समुद्रश्च हिमवांश्च व्यशीर्यत।
en: All the luminaries became deprived of their effulgence. The Creator, Brahman, himself dropped from his seat. The Ocean himself became dry. The mountains of Himavat became riven.

sa: यदक्षरमथाव्यक्तमीशं लोकस्य भावनम्॥ कूटस्थं कर्तृ निर्द्वन्द्वमकर्तेति च यं विदुः। व्यक्तिभावगतस्यास्य एका मूर्तिरियं शुभा॥ नरो नारायणश्चैव जातौ ,धर्मकुलोद्वहौ।
en: That which is indestructible, immutable, supreme, the origin of the universe, uniform, and the supreme actor, that which is above all pairs of opposites, and inactive, has, chosing to be shown, been pleased to assume this one blessed form. This Nara and Narayana have taken birth in the race of Dharma.

sa: त्वं चैव क्रोधजस्तात पूर्वसर्गे सनातनः॥ मया च सार्धं वरद विबुधैश्च महर्षिभिः। प्रसादयाशु लोकानां शान्तिर्भवतु मा चिरम्॥
en: Eternal as you are, for you have ever existed since all the past creations, you too have originated from His anger. With myself then, these gods, and all the great Rishis, do you worship this displayed form of Brahma and let peace be to all the worlds forthwith!

sa: शयनं चैकपाāन दिवसानेकविंशतिम्। अकिंचिदुक्त्वा गमनं बहिश्च मुनिपुङ्गवा॥
en: O foremost of ascetics, what also was your object, again in going out of the room without speaking a single word.

sa: प्रासादानां बहूनां च काञ्चनानां महामुने। पणिविद्रुमपादानां पर्याणां च दर्शनम्॥
en: What, indeed, was your motive in showing, O great ascetic, so many palaces made of gold and so many bedsteads supported on posts of jewels and gems?

sa: उत्थाय चास्मि निष्क्रान्तो यदि मां त्वं महीपते। पृच्छेः क्व यास्यसीत्येवं शपेयं त्वामिति प्रभो॥
en: Rising from my bed I went out of the chamber without speaking to any of you. I did this, O king, in the hope that you would ask me and thus I would have an opportunity of cursing you.

sa: पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यामि समेषु विषमेषु च। त्वामहं नरशार्दूल गच्छन्तमनिवर्तितुम्॥
en: O best of men, I shall follow you over even and uneven ground. Going with you, I shall never return again.

sa: धिग्धार्तराष्ट्र सुनृशंसबुद्धिं धिक् सौबलं पापमतिं च कर्णम्। अनर्थमिच्छन्ति नरेन्द्र पापा येधर्मनित्यस्य सतस्तवैवम्॥
en: Fie on the cruel-hearted son of Dhritarashtra! Fie on the evil-minded son of Subala (Shakuni)! Fie on Karna! O ruler of men, those sinful wretches always wish evil to you who are so firm in virtue.

sa: यथा चात्मनि कल्याणं सम्भावयसि पाण्डव। सहस्रगुणमप्येतत् त्वयि सम्भावयाम्यहम्॥
en: What good you yourself consider possible to do to the Pandavas, I consider it possible for you to do a thousand times of that.

sa: यदन्यद् दिष्टभावस्य पुरुषस्य स्वयं कृतम्। तस्मादनुपरोधश्च विद्यते तत्र लक्षणम्॥
en: Over and above the actions that a man is destined to perform, he can do away with others as well at his will; which the Shastras testify.

sa: तां तु रक्षस्तदा ब्रह्मन् हृच्छयेनाभिपीडितम्। दृष्ट्वा हृष्टमभूद्राजन् जिहीर्षुस्तामनिन्दिताम्॥
en: O Rishi, the Rakshasa, having seen her, burnt in lust. He was very much delighted and he determined to carry away the irreproachable lady.

sa: पश्चादिमां पिता प्रादाद्धगवेऽनृतकारकः। सेयं यदि वरारोहा भृगोर्भार्या रहोगता॥
en: was a But her vile father subsequently gave her to Bhrigu. (Tell me truly) if she can be truly called the wife of Bhrigu.

sa: नारद उवाच हिरण्यपुरमित्येतत् ख्यात् पुरवरं महत्। दैत्यानां दानवानां च मायाशतविचारिणाम्॥
en: Narada said This excellent and spacious city is known by the name of Hiranyapura. It is the city of the Daityas and the Danavas, who practice a hundred different illusions,

sa: मातलिस्त्वब्रवीदेनं भाषमाणं तथाविधम्। देवर्षे नैव मे कार्य विप्रियं त्रिदिवौकसाम्॥
en: Matali then said to him who spoke thus, "O celestial Rishi, I cannot do what would not be to the liking of the dwellers of the heaven.

sa: मार्कण्डेय उवाच उपविष्टं तु तं स्कन्दं हिरण्यकवचस्रजम्। हिरण्यचूडमुकुटं हिरण्याक्षं महाप्रभम्॥
en: Markandeya said : Skanda was adorned with a golden armlet and garland; he wore a crest and crown of gold; his eyes were gold coloured and they were very bright.

sa: ऋषय ऊचुः हिरण्यगर्भ भद्रं ते लोकानां शङ्करो भव। त्वया षड्राजजातेन सर्वे लोका वशीकृताः॥
en: The Rishis said: O golden egg-born one, may prosperity come to you. May you be the cause of doing good to the world. Though you have been born in six nights, all the worlds have come to your subjection.

sa: अनुप्रविश्य रुद्रेण वह्नि जातो ह्ययं शिशुः। तत्र जातस्ततः स्कन्दो रुद्रसूनुस्ततोऽभवत्॥
en: The child had his birth from the action of Rudra entering into the constitution of the deity of fire and for this reasort Skanda is called the son of Rudra.

sa: अग्निं ते ददृशुस्तत्र स्थितं शैलमिवाग्रतः। मार्गमावृत्य तिष्ठन्तं साक्षात्पुरुषविग्रहम्॥
en: The Pandavas there saw the God of Fire standing before them like hill. Closing their way, the god stood there in his embodied form.

sa: त्वया हि मे प्रणुन्नस्य गतिरन्या न विद्यते। तृष्णाशोकश्रमाणां हि त्वं काम प्रभवः सदा॥
en: If I continue to be unruffled by you, O desire, I shall necessarily be without a path (by which to effect my salvation). You O desire, are always the parent of thirst, of sorrow, and of fatigue and toil.

sa: प्रहाय कामं लोभं च सुखं प्राप्तोऽस्मि साम्प्रतम्। नाद्य लोभवशं प्राप्तो दुःखं प्राप्स्याम्यनात्मवान्॥
en: Having renounced Desire and Cupidity, my happiness has now been great. I shall no longer surrender myself to the influence of Cupidity, nor shall I undergo the pangs of misery like a person of impure soul.

sa: एवमेतद् यथाऽऽत्थ त्वमात्मानं परमेश्वर। दुष्टुमिच्छामि ते रूपमैश्वरं पुरुषोत्तम॥
en: O great Lord, what you have said yourself is even so (perfectly true). I desire to see, O best of beings, your divine form.
